title: The last five units
summary: Prevent overselling when independent workers reserve stock concurrently.

stages.title: Understand the contract
stages.brief: Prevent overselling when independent workers reserve stock concurrently. Preserve the documented public interface. Use only Python 3.11 standard-library modules.
requirements: Preserve InventoryStore methods __init__, seed, available, reserve, and close. seed is an administrative fixture used before requests; it need not support concurrent reseeding.
reserve(sku, quantity) returns True exactly when stock was reduced by that quantity; otherwise returns False with no stock change for a missing SKU or insufficient stock.
Across independent SQLite connections to one database, total successful reserved quantity must never exceed seeded stock, and remaining stock must match the successful reservations.
Reject non-string/whitespace-only SKU and non-positive/non-integer quantity with ValueError before any change. Booleans are invalid quantities.

Use durable database coordination, not a process-local lock. The same database must retain remaining stock after reopening. Each worker owns its connection; do not share SQLite connections between threads.

stages.title: Implement the change
stages.brief: Make the smallest coherent change that satisfies the disclosed contract.
requirements: Preserve public interfaces and existing valid behavior.

stages.title: Verify the behavior
stages.brief: Run checks and inspect failures before finishing.
requirements: Run public checks and add a targeted boundary or regression check.
Identify behavior that your tests do not establish.

stages.title: Defend your decisions
stages.brief: Explain the submitted code and its remaining limits.
requirements: Use concrete code or test evidence.
Describe one alternative and its trade-off.

rubric.name: Atomic reservation
rubric.description: Keep the read/check/write invariant under concurrency.

anchors.strong: Uses a transaction or conditional database operation that coordinates independent connections and explains the serialization point.
anchors.developing: Sequential behavior works but atomicity is unverified or a race remains.
anchors.needsWork: Uses check-then-write or only a local lock and assumes separate workers cannot oversell.

rubric.name: Consistency and failures
rubric.description: Preserve stock and API behavior for all outcomes.

anchors.strong: Rejects invalid quantities, leaves unsuccessful requests unchanged, and preserves persisted counts.
anchors.developing: Common success works but failure/type semantics have a gap.
anchors.needsWork: Accepts negative reservations, loses updates, or returns success without the corresponding stock change.

rubric.name: Concurrency evidence
rubric.description: Test actual independent connections and acknowledge limits.

anchors.strong: Tests concurrent accepted counts against persisted stock and explains why one passing stress run alone is not a proof.
anchors.developing: Runs threads but does not check the invariant or uses one shared connection.
anchors.needsWork: Uses sequential tests as the only evidence of concurrent safety.

probes.question: Where is the operation that prevents two workers from both spending the last unit?
What happens to stock and the return value on insufficient inventory or an invalid quantity?
What does your concurrency test establish, and what can a successful stress run still fail to prove?

hints: Write the invariant relating seeded stock, accepted quantities, and remaining stock. Then inspect where the current method reads and writes.
A separate connection can read the same old count before either worker writes. A Python lock does not coordinate another process.
A conditional UPDATE can decrement only where available >= quantity; its affected-row count tells you whether that atomic operation succeeded.

drills.title: Identify a serialization point
drills.lesson: Atomic state changes and concurrent invariants
drills.exercise: For 5 units and 12 buyers, specify the allowed success count and final stock. Write a schedule that breaks read-then-write and an atomic alternative.

drills.title: Account for every accepted unit
drills.exercise: Seed seven units, perform accepted and rejected reservations of different sizes, and verify seeded = accepted + remaining. Include negative, boolean, and missing-SKU requests.

drills.title: Test independent connections
drills.lesson: Concurrent testing and the limits of stress tests
drills.exercise: Start multiple workers with separate database connections and a common start barrier. Check accepted quantity and final count together. Explain a stale-read schedule and why one passing run is not a proof.
